subject: Game Theory
title: The Vickrey Auction
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Vickrey Auction.

hook.text: You win a painting at auction for $1,000—but you only pay $800, the second-highest bid. Why does this work?

buildup.text: The Vickrey auction (sealed-bid, second-price): highest bidder wins but pays the second-highest bid amount.

discovery.text: This makes truth-telling dominant: bid your true value, because you'll never pay what you bid—only the next bid down.

twist.text: Bidding higher than your value risks overpaying. Bidding lower risks losing. Your true value is always safest.

climax.text: William Vickrey won the 1996 Nobel Prize. Google's ad system uses his second-price logic billions of times daily.

punchline.text: Pay what the runner-up would have paid.

quiz.question: Why is bidding your true value optimal in a Vickrey auction?
options: You pay the second-highest bid, so overbidding risks loss
